analysis:
I examined the new in-memory prompt-token cache (PromptTokenCache.swift), the new optional-scope branch in ProviderPromptContractPipeline.tokenize (head lines 39-58), and the decode refactor in ProviderLoop+InboundDecode.swift. I found no concrete regression.

PromptTokenCache (relevant to T-041, A-001, TB-007): pieces are keyed by SHA-256 over a domain tag, the length-prefixed scope and the piece bytes (scopedHasher, lines 476-482). Tenants in different scopes therefore cannot share entries or observe each other through tokenization speed. The store is memory-only, with nothing written to disk, so it adds no at-rest artifact. It is bounded: 32 MiB by default, a hard cap of 4096 MiB via env, and a per-entry cap of capacity/8. Stored token IDs are derived from plaintext prompts and live only in process memory, which fits the existing T-011/T-014 operator-memory assumptions. The tokenization-time oracle stays within one scope, which matches the accepted same-account SEC-035 channel.

The splitter declines (returns nil) for lstrip/rstrip tokens, overlapping added tokens and non-identity post-processors. A load-time self-check and sampled background verification disable the cache on any mismatch. A crafted prompt that caused a mismatch could disable the cache for a model, which costs performance only. The verification task retains plaintext messages until it runs, which is bounded and in-process.

Open integration questions (hence needs_deeper_review=true):
1. The callers that supply promptCacheScope are not in the supplied evidence. They must pass the coordinator-authored cacheSalt, never a caller-controlled value, and nil whenever the prefix cache is off.
2. decodeInboundChatRequest calls repairedRequestBody without modelType. This skips the GLM raw-control validation and the GLM schema-preservation branch that decodeOpenAIRequest(modelType:) applies. If admission previously passed a modelType for GLM models, this would be a behavior change. The doc comment implies the model-blind shape was the old behavior, but I could not confirm it.
3. In InboundChatExtensions, each field decodes independently and extensions are taken from the original bytes, as before. Semantics appear preserved.

No changes to the attestation, authorization or encryption boundaries were observed.
